title: Microsoft testing Remote Lock for lost or stolen Windows devices
content_md: Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets enterprise IT administrators remotely lock stolen or lost Windows devices without wiping them. Named Remote Lock, this new feature is shipping to devices upgraded to Windows 11 Insider Preview builds in the Beta ( Build 26320.10003 ) and Experimental ( Build 26340.10013 ) channels. Admins can use Microsoft Intune custom configuration profiles to lock Microsoft Entra-joined, hybrid-joined, or MDM-enrolled devices that run Windows Enterprise, Education, or Pro. After the IT department remotely locks the device, the system can only be unlocked via Intune, since PINs, passwords, local admins, or web sign-ins will no longer work. Microsoft added that the user's credentials will remain valid and can still be used to sign into other devices that haven't been locked. "Windows signs out every active session, hides all sign-in options and shows a locked screen," said Windows Insider communications lead Stephen Lines . "Nothing is erased: the device stays enrolled and managed, BitLocker stays on and user data stays in place. The lock holds across restarts and while offline, and only an admin can lift it remotely, so the user picks up where they left off."
